About twelve years ago, I had a job at a grocery store, and I did a lot of walking on a hard tile floor. I think I asked to take a whole week off once, and I tried all kinds of products. I tried hard arch supports that felt like walking around with a block of wood in my shoe. It just made my foot hurt elsewhere. Dr. Scholls is all crap. I found some shoes were better than others, but my heels still hurt. I insisted on New Balance and Dunham shoes and found Hydrofeet inserts to be quite nice. My heels were still hurting. So I lived with the idea that I needed to limit the amount of walking I did and running and jogging were certainly out of the question. It has been over 10 years like this.

Recently, I haven't had much to do living in a new place. Before I left where I was previously, I had a good friend I would go workout with occasionally. He had a shed with workout equipment in it. After some time here, I decided to get a gym membership, and now I go almost everyday. I do 16 minutes of HIIT on a bike every 2-3 days. I also have 3 different days of weight lifting that's about an hour each day. I would say I repeat the 3 days twice per week and take a day off sometimes, not always.

Now that I've been doing this for about 2 months, I've found my heels are not hurting like they used to. Thinking of things I haven't done before with my heel problem, it seems to be the calf machine that is making the difference. I also happened to start this exercise late. I decided to do it during resting from bench presses since it's right next to the bench. I've also had a problem with just tired achy feet in general, and now my feet are feeling great. I'm still trying to comprehend living without heel and feet pain like I used to have, because I became so accustomed to just living with it.

A few notes:

A doctor can't do much for this problem. They can give you a cortisol shot if it gets really bad, and they try to make custom inserts. They're actually very expensive with a hit or miss kind of success rate.

I'm not overweight and acquired the problem when I was my normal high school and after weigh (skinny/BMI 19) or even thinner. Recently, I had picked up a little belly fat from sitting too much. Now it's going away since I started working again, and I am working out now too. My point is my foot problems weren't the result of carrying around 100 lbs of lard on me.
